en: The Section on Detailed Exposition, Chapter Three: Convergence (Sampāta)
The Convergence of the Mode of Conveying Reasoning:
Therein, what is the convergence of the mode of conveying reasoning?
“Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded...”
Having right intention as one's range,
with right view as the foremost,
and having understood arising and passing away;
“The monk who has overcome sloth and torpor abandons all miserable destinies.
Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded, right intention is the pasture. For one whose mind is guarded, right intention is the pasture.
"It will come to be" is logical; "right view will have right intention as its domain" is logical;
"dwelling with right view as his primary concern, he will penetrate arising and passing away" is logical; "penetrating arising and passing away, he will abandon all miserable destinies" is logical.
"Abandoning all miserable destinies, he will transcend all fears of miserable destinies and states of perdition"—this is logical.
Thus ends the section on the "Method of Logical Connection."
